data.summary: The mgr directory is the packaging and deployment shell for `aio-mgr`, the sandbox-mgr control plane that manages multi-sandbox lifecycle from a single axum server. It contains the crate manifest (Cargo.toml), the container build recipe (Dockerfile), and the independent Docker Compose stack (compose.yml) that runs the control plane either bare-metal or containerized against the host Docker daemon. Together these files define how the control-plane binary is declared, built, and launched; the actual Rust service logic lives in the sibling source subdirectory.

file_insights.name: Cargo.toml
file_insights.summary: Cargo manifest for the `aio-mgr` crate, declaring it as a member of the root workspace and pulling in the aio-config and aio-models path crates plus the axum/tokio web stack. The comments document that the same binary runs in two forms (bare-metal host process or containerized stack) and that all Docker interaction happens through the CLI, never the Docker API.
file_insights.source_summary: A standard Cargo package section declaring name = "aio-mgr", version 0.1.0, edition 2021, and a description of the multi-sandbox lifecycle manager. The body is largely design commentary: it explains the two execution forms (bare-metal vs containerized), the requirement that all Docker interaction goes through the `docker` / `docker compose` CLI, and the workspace/path-crate relationship with aio-config and aio-models.
file_insights.detailed_description: This is the build and dependency contract for the sandbox-mgr control plane. It fixes the crate name (`aio-mgr`), edition, and description, and records the Phase 1 design decision that the mgr-api axum server must be runnable both as a bare-metal `cargo run -p aio-mgr` process and as a container in the mgr compose stack, with all docker/compose interaction going through the CLI usable from either context. Because it is a workspace member resolved from the repo root, it anchors the cross-crate dependency edges that the Dockerfile then has to preserve at build time.
responsibilities: Declare the aio-mgr crate identity, version, and edition
Pin the third-party runtime dependencies (axum server, async runtime) for the control plane
Declare workspace-relative dependencies on the aio-config and aio-models path crates
Document the dual bare-metal/container execution requirement and CLI-only Docker access policy

file_insights.name: Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Multi-stage container build recipe for the aio-mgr axum server, using the official Rust image as both builder and runtime since mgr has no scenario-derived base image. The build context is the repo root (mirroring app/Dockerfile) so the root cargo workspace and the aio-config/aio-models path crates resolve correctly.
file_insights.source_summary: Begins with the `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` directive, followed by comments explaining that the build context is the repository root, that mgr depends on the aio-config and aio-models path crates as a workspace member, and that unlike app there is no scenario-derived base image. The stages then build the Rust workspace and produce a self-contained axum server image capable of running against a mounted Docker socket.
file_insights.detailed_description: The Dockerfile packages the plain, self-contained control-plane server into an image that the mgr compose stack can run. It intentionally uses the repo root as build context (`context: ..` with `dockerfile: mgr/Dockerfile`) because mgr is a cargo workspace member that depends on path crates, and it is explicitly contrasted with app/Dockerfile, which does have a scenario-derived base image. Since the mgr runtime shells out to `docker` / `docker compose`, the resulting image must be built so it can be paired with a mounted host Docker socket at runtime.
responsibilities: Build the aio-mgr crate from the repo-root cargo workspace context
Resolve workspace path dependencies (aio-config, aio-models) during the image build
Produce a self-contained runtime image for the axum control-plane server
Keep the image compatible with the DooD (Docker-out-of-Docker) socket-mount deployment model

file_insights.name: compose.yml
file_insights.summary: Defines the independent `aio-mgr` Compose project that brings up the sandbox-mgr control plane alongside the existing sandbox stacks. It mounts the host Docker socket and stresses path identity because mgr-api invokes `docker compose` and `docker build` as subprocesses with relative paths resolved against the host.
file_insights.source_summary: Comment headers describe the sandbox-mgr control-plane stack, the `aio-mgr` project name, the `make mgr-up` entry point from the repo root, and the guarantee that it is a pure addition to the existing sandbox stacks. Service definitions run the mgr-api container with the host Docker socket mounted (DooD) and build from the repo root using mgr/Dockerfile, with comments warning that path identity is load-bearing for the relative paths inside the sandbox compose files it drives.
file_insights.detailed_description: This is the Phase 2 deployment descriptor for the control-plane stack, deliberately isolated as its own Compose project (started via `make mgr-up` with an explicit `-p` project name and file path) so it never interferes with the existing sandbox stacks. The load-bearing detail is path identity: mgr-api runs `docker compose` and `docker build` against the host daemon through the mounted `/var/run/docker.sock`, so the sandbox compose files it drives must contain relative paths that resolve correctly from the host filesystem. It also declares the build context as the repo root with `dockerfile: mgr/Dockerfile`, tying the runtime stack back to the workspace-aware image build.
responsibilities: Declare the standalone `aio-mgr` Compose project for the control plane
Wire the mgr-api service to the host Docker daemon via the mounted /var/run/docker.sock (DooD)
Set the build context to the repo root with `dockerfile: mgr/Dockerfile`
Preserve host path identity so relative paths in the driven sandbox compose files resolve correctly
Provide the `make mgr-up` startup path without touching existing sandbox stacks
